checks.invariant: Only the owning area author/Admin may edit a question graph; accepted references preserve answer-parent binding, and graph-derived changes preserve saved evidence without granting specification or requirement access.
checks.result: Visibility PUT:18-40 uses the area-author mutation policy; assignment-authorization.ts:580-625 resolves the stored owning area and :697-702 enforces it. Schemas:33-55 bound graph shape. DAL:1767-1918 normalizes duplicate edges, binds answers to parents and rejects snapshot-visible cycles; migration0027 adds foreign keys and uniqueness. DAL:2013-2083 transacts graph replacement with affected-descendant history marking; :1963-2008 limits updates to affected current answers and preserves rows/actor attribution. ADR0022 explicitly permits cross-area references and stewardship propagation, so absence of per-specification authorship on this path is intentional. DAL:1680-1740 recomputes visibility; :2300-2345 excludes hidden/inactive answers from filter effects. service-specifications.ts:342-401 separately authorizes specification reads and applies selection only as an explicit published-requirement filter. Per-specification answer workflow:65-115 authorizes the specification and transacts mutation/audit; DAL:2210-2273 requires confirmation before hidden-answer historical marking. Hierarchy display uses visited sets, not authorization. Tests:632-814 document cross-area descendant preservation; read only. Concurrent graph changes lack an explicit common lock, but no source-established security boundary failure survives independent authorization and visibility recomputation.

hardening: DAL:1150-1184 and :1456-1492 mark only directly changed question/answer selections historical when deactivating or archiving; unlike visibility replacement, they do not run descendant-history propagation. ADR0022 requires newly hidden saved descendants to become historical. Current read/filter paths still recompute visibility and exclude hidden answers, so this is a lifecycle correctness issue rather than an established authorization bypass; review restoration semantics before changing it.

Graph validation at DAL:1866-1918 reads a snapshot before replacement, and history marking races with ordinary answer writes without an explicit shared graph/specification lock. An isolated concurrency regression would clarify cycle/history consistency. No runtime schedule, deadlock, or unauthorized result was observed because target execution is prohibited.
